dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise.

Hi, Denise, good morning. My name is Carmen Valdez, and I'm calling because, okay, so I walk to my shop every morning, I've got a little place and I've had it for years, and I park in the same spot and then I walk the rest of the way, which takes me right past the school. And last weekend we had that snow that turned to rain, the Sunday into Monday one, and now it's Wednesday.
Okay, I'm with you. Which sidewalk are we talking about?

The one along the school. The sidewalk on the side by the front drive, where the kids get dropped off. It was never cleared. Not Monday, not Tuesday, and this morning it's this gray slushy ice, because it froze overnight. I'm not exaggerating, it's just a sheet.
Ugh, yeah, that slush turns to concrete once it freezes. Is it the school's own walkway or the public sidewalk out along the street?

The public one, along the street. The plow came down the road, I'll give them that, but it pushed everything up onto the sidewalk and then nobody touched it. So it's a wall of it, and then ice on top. Kids are walking in the road around it. I saw two of them this morning doing that.
That's not good with the cars coming through at drop-off. Let me get some details so I can send it to the right crew. Is there a cross street or a landmark you'd use?

Well, it's the school, that's the landmark. The front of it. I don't have a house number, I'm not at a house, I'm walking past. Anyway, what I'd like is for a plow to come back. Or whoever does the sidewalks. Somebody with the little machine. Because the big truck already came and obviously that wasn't enough.
Understood. I'll put in a request for a return pass and sidewalk clearing along the front of the school. Sometimes the sidewalks are a separate crew from the roads, so I'll flag both.

Thank you. And I'll tell you, it's not just me. My neighbor, she runs a tiny bakery out of her kitchen, and she has people coming for pickup, mostly older folks, and she called me yesterday saying nobody can get to her end of the street either. So she's stuck with loaves nobody can come get.
Oh no. Is her street one you can name? I can add that as a second spot.
I'd rather not give her street without asking her. I'm sorry, I know that's annoying. Just the school one for now.
That's fine, no problem. If she wants it checked she can call us herself. Do you want a call back when the crew's been out?
Yes, please, because this is the second day I've called about something like this and I'd like to know somebody actually went. My number is 401-555-0169.
Got it, 401-555-0169. And it's Carmen?
Carmen Valdez, with a V. V-A-L-D-E-Z.

Perfect. I've got the school front sidewalk, never cleared after Sunday-Monday's storm, now iced over, request for a plow or sidewalk crew to return. I'll mark it as a safety concern since kids are walking in the road.
Good. Because the rain was supposed to wash it away and it just didn't. It's been three days of this.
I hear you. With the freeze last night it's probably worse than Monday. Crews should get to the priority spots like schools first, so you'll likely hear back today or tomorrow.
Okay. I'll believe it when I see it, but okay. Thanks, Denise.
You're welcome, Carmen. Watch your step walking in.
